note: After the Battle of Köse Dağ (1243), the Sultanate of Rum becomes a vassal of the Ilkhanate. Seljuk sultans rule in name but require Mongol approval; the Ilkhanate extracts tribute and military service. This dependence accelerates the sultanate's fragmentation into rival Turkic beyliks.

_quarry.structural_significance: Mongol overlordship of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum fragmented Anatolian political authority into competing Turkish beyliks that were too small to resist individually but too numerous to consolidate; this political fragmentation was the direct structural condition enabling the tiny Ottoman beylik's opportunistic expansion—without Mongol atomisation, a more unified Anatolia might have checked Ottoman growth.
